slides.title: Pluralistic Human-Robot Interaction: Designing for Robot Interaction with Diverse Communities
slides.tldr: FRAMEWORK FOR INCLUSIVE SOCIAL ROBOT INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a Pluralistic HRI framework to address social complexity and human diversity in real-world deployments, supporting the RwB goal of embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Proposes a Pluralistic HRI framework to treat human diversity as a foundational social robot design concern.
card.key_idea: A framework integrating seven principles: pluralism, civic dialogue, perspective-taking, empathy, intercultural competence, cultural humility, and moral imagination to create inclusive, adaptive, and ethically grounded interactions.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper outlines proposed evaluation metrics (e.g., inclusion, dialogue quality) rather than reporting experimental results.
card.limitation: Risks include reinforcing stereotypes, excluding non-normative users, and privileging dominant cultural assumptions if pluralistic principles are not implemented.

slides.title: Galaxy General Unveils Self-Learning Humanoid Robot
slides.highlight: The introduction of a self-learning humanoid robot reflects the 'one brain, many skills' inflection point in embodied AI, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Rethinking the Evaluation and Optimization of LLM-Based Social Simulation
slides.tldr: IMPROVING LLM SOCIAL SIMULATION FIDELITY VIA SUBJECTIVITY-ADAPTIVE TRAINING
slides.highlight: This work proposes a subjectivity coefficient and Subjectivity-Adaptive soft-Label Training (SALT) to better model the inherent subjectivity of human behavior in social simulations, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation using LLM-based agents.

card.one_liner: SALT improves LLM social simulation by replacing hard-label training with subjectivity-adaptive soft labels based on semantic similarity.
card.key_idea: Introduces a subjectivity coefficient to quantify behavioral randomness and uses it to adaptively size neighborhoods for aggregating similar contexts into soft distributional labels.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new SubjSim benchmark (19,300 pairs) using Qwen3-8B; SALT significantly reduced KL, JSD, TVD, and MMD compared to SFT.
card.limitation: In very low-subjectivity regimes, pooling neighbors can blur sharp targets, potentially making it less effective than standard SFT.

slides.title: Closing the Affective Loop: Multimodal Speaker-Listener Emotion-Dynamics-Aware Empathetic Social Robots
slides.highlight: This work introduces AffectLoop, which tracks speaker verbal and facial affective dynamics alongside the listener's state to improve embodied empathetic interaction, aligning with HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: AffectLoop improves social robot empathy by conditioning LLM responses on both speaker and listener affective dynamics.
card.key_idea: A multimodal system tracking speaker verbal/facial VAD trajectories and robot affective states to generate congruent spoken responses and embodied behaviors via GPT-4.1-nano.
card.evaluation: Pilot within-subject study (5 participants) using Likert scales and log analysis. Proposed system showed higher user satisfaction and stronger valence-based distress recovery.
card.limitation: Preliminary results based on a very small sample size of five participants in a pilot study.

slides.title: Study Explores Impact on Trust When Expressive Humanoid Robots Make Mistakes
slides.highlight: This study examines how expressive humanoid robots affect user trust when errors occur, providing insights for RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Collective Counterfactual Planning: Coordination, Consent, and Verification under Representational Constraints
slides.tldr: FORMAL MODEL FOR COLLECTIVE PLANNING UNDER REPRESENTATIONAL CONSTRAINTS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a formal model for Collective Counterfactual Planning where agents operate within agent-specific subspaces, providing a framework for analyzing coordination and verification in multi-agent systems relevant to MIMIC's societal-scale simulations.

card.one_liner: A formal model of collective planning where agent limitations are defined by representational subspace geometry.
card.key_idea: Introduces Collective Counterfactual Planning (CCP) using four gates—implementation, conception, consent, and verification—to determine if a team can conceive, execute, and validate a goal.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via machine-checked numerical examples (E1, E2) and formal theorems proving solvability dualities and consent-model incomparability.
card.limitation: The model is non-strategic, assuming agents are truthful, share the goal, and consent mechanically.

slides.title: HODAgent: Towards On-Demand, Responsive Humanoids for Physical World Human Interaction
slides.highlight: HODAgent introduces a System-2 architecture for humanoid robots to handle responsive execution and task revision during human interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: HODAgent is a System-2 embodied agent enabling responsive, on-demand human-humanoid interaction in simulated and physical environments.
card.key_idea: A semi-duplex architecture coordinating an Env-Interactor, Planner, Executor, and hierarchical Memory to handle requests and replan during active physical execution via an embodiment-independent interface.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a workflow-conditioned User Agent in simulation (164 cases) and on a Unitree G1 robot; outperformed ReAct baselines in Joint Success.
card.limitation: Does not provide full-duplex or hard real-time interaction guarantees, broad cross-robot generalization, or task-level sim-to-real transfer.

slides.title: Learning Varying Physical Therapist-Patient Interactions for Robot-mediated Upper Limb Task-Specific Training
slides.tldr: LEARNING PERSONALIZED THERAPIST-PATIENT INTERACTIONS FOR REHABILITATION ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a Learning-from-Demonstration framework to capture personalized physical therapist-patient interactions, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: A framework to learn and generalize personalized therapist-patient physical interactions for robot-mediated upper limb rehabilitation.
card.key_idea: Uses Task-Parameterised Gaussian Mixture Models (TPGMM) to map patient joint kinematics to therapist-applied torques, generalizing learned interactions to unseen task variations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using 14 mock therapist-patient pairs across three tasks. TPGMM was compared against a Look-Up Table (LUT) using reconstruction error and coverage.
card.limitation: Reproduced interactions in unseen variations deviated slightly from actual interactions, though accuracy improved as task complexity increased.

slides.title: Classifying Directional Trajectories Near Criticality in the Three-State Majority-Vote Model with Deep Belief Networks and Bidirectional GRUs
slides.tldr: CLASSIFYING CRITICAL TRANSITIONS IN OPINION DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a hierarchical DBN and Bi-GRU architecture to classify directional trajectories and detect critical transitions in agent-based opinion dynamics, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: A DBN-Bi-GRU pipeline classifies directional trajectories near criticality in the three-state majority-vote model.
card.key_idea: A Deep Belief Network encodes lattice snapshots into latent vectors, which a Bidirectional GRU then processes as sequences to classify four trajectory types.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 1,200 synthetic trajectories using t-SNE and accuracy; achieved 0.99 test accuracy, outperforming a PCA-based baseline (0.854).
card.limitation: DBN training on static samples may miss non-equilibrium features; results are limited to a finite 28x28 lattice.
